servers.name: Atlas Scientific EZO Sensors
servers.protocol: Atlas Scientific EZO UART command set
servers.summary: Read pH, ORP, dissolved oxygen, conductivity/TDS/salinity, temperature, humidity, CO2 or pressure; calibrate, set temperature compensation, log series.
servers.description: MCP server for Atlas Scientific EZO sensor circuits (pH, ORP, DO, EC, RTD, HUM, CO2, PRS) over UART: read, calibrate, compensate, log.

tools.name: calibrate
tools.description: Store one calibration point. The probe must already be in the named standard (buffer, air, dry, ...) with a stable reading. Point names are validated per circuit type. pH: a `mid` calibration erases existing low/high points, so always do mid first. EC: do `dry` first.

tools.name: clear_calibration
tools.description: Delete all stored calibration data (Cal,clear). pH/ORP/DO/EC/RTD return to uncalibrated; CO2/PRS return to their factory calibration. The probe must be recalibrated afterwards.

tools.name: get_calibration_status
tools.description: Report how many calibration points are stored and what that means for this circuit type; for pH also the probe slope (acid/base % of ideal and zero offset in mV).

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: get_info
tools.description: Report the circuit type, firmware, device name, supply voltage and last restart reason, LED state, calibration state, temperature compensation and type-specific settings (enabled outputs, EC probe constant K, DO salinity/pressure compensation).

tools.name: log_series
tools.description: Record a series of readings (e.g. to watch a probe stabilise before calibrating, follow pH or DO in a bioreactor, or log temperature). Returns every point plus mean, stdev, min, max and drift per minute for each output.

tools.name: read_value
tools.description: Take one reading (about 1 s) and return every enabled output with its unit: pH; ORP in mV; DO in mg/L (and % saturation if enabled); EC in µS/cm plus TDS (ppm), salinity (PSU) and specific gravity if enabled; RTD temperature; humidity %RH (+ air temperature, dew point); CO2 ppm; or pressure.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: set_do_compensation
tools.description: DO circuits only: set salinity compensation (irrelevant below ~2500 µS/cm) and/or atmospheric pressure compensation (default 101.3 kPa; lower at altitude). Neither is retained through a power cycle.

tools.name: set_led
tools.description: Turn the circuit's status LED on or off. Returns the new LED state.

tools.name: set_probe_constant
tools.description: EC circuits only: set the conductivity probe's cell constant K to match the probe (printed on it). Recalibrate after changing it. Returns the K now in use.

tools.name: set_temperature_compensation
tools.description: Set the sample temperature used to compensate pH, EC or DO readings (T,n; always °C). Not retained through a power cycle. Returns the value the circuit now uses.

servers.name: Micro-Manager Microscope
servers.vendor: Micro-Manager (open source; hundreds of camera, stage, filter and light-source vendors)
models: Any microscope with a Micro-Manager hardware configuration (.cfg)
interfaces: Camera Link / CoaXPress / GigE (through Micro-Manager device adapters)
servers.summary: Snap images (stats + preview + TIFF), z-stacks and time-lapses, move XY/Z within step and soft limits, channel/objective presets, exposure, shutter, autofocus.
servers.description: MCP server for microscopes controlled by Micro-Manager (pymmcore-plus): snap images, z-stacks and time-lapses, move stages safely, switch channels and objectives, autofocus.

tools.name: acquire_time_lapse
tools.description: Acquire a time-lapse at the current position: images every `interval_s` (optionally several channels per timepoint), saves a multi-page TIFF and reports per-frame statistics and the intensity change (bleaching). Bounded by `max_frames` and `max_acquisition_duration_s`; `stop_stage` aborts it.

tools.name: acquire_z_stack
tools.description: Acquire a z-stack around the current focus: moves Z through the slices (optionally imaging several channels at each), saves a multi-page TIFF, reports per-slice statistics and the sharpest slice, and returns Z to where it started. Every slice must stay within `max_z_step_um` of the start and the Z soft limits.

tools.name: autofocus
tools.description: Run the configured autofocus device (e.g. a hardware focus lock) once; it moves the focus drive. If the result is outside the Z step or soft limits, the focus is moved back and an error is raised.

tools.name: close_shutter
tools.description: Close the shutter (stop illuminating the sample) and abort any running acquisition.

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: get_exposure
tools.description: Return the camera exposure time in milliseconds.

tools.name: get_position
tools.description: Read the XY stage and focus (Z) positions in micrometres, and which way increasing Z moves the objective.

tools.name: get_system_info
tools.description: Describe the microscope: loaded devices (camera, stages, shutters, filter wheels...), which device has which role, camera size/bit depth/exposure, pixel size, config groups with their presets, the current position, and the soft limits. Call this first.

tools.name: list_config_groups
tools.description: List Micro-Manager config groups (e.g. Channel, Objective) with their presets and the preset currently active.

tools.name: move_stage_xy
tools.description: Move the XY stage. Moves longer than `max_xy_step_um` or outside the XY soft limits are refused before anything moves. Make sure the objective and condenser clear the sample holder.

tools.name: move_z
tools.description: Move the focus drive (Z). Moving the objective toward the sample can crash it into the slide: moves larger than `max_z_step_um` or outside the Z soft limits are refused before anything moves.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: set_config
tools.description: Apply a config-group preset (e.g. switch the channel: filter cube, light source, emission filter). Objective/turret groups are refused here: use `set_objective`.

tools.name: set_exposure
tools.description: Set the camera exposure time (ms). Longer exposures give brighter images but more photobleaching. Returns the exposure the camera accepted.

tools.name: set_objective
tools.description: Switch the objective (rotates the nosepiece/turret). A longer or immersion objective can hit the sample holder or need oil/water: confirm with the user first. Pixel size changes with the objective.

tools.name: set_shutter
tools.description: Open or close the current shutter, and optionally switch auto-shutter. An open shutter illuminates (and bleaches) the sample until it is closed again.

tools.name: snap_image
tools.description: Acquire one image with the current channel, exposure and position. The sample is illuminated during the exposure. Saves the full image as TIFF and returns summary statistics (min/max/mean, saturation, sharpness) plus an optional contrast-stretched preview.

tools.name: stop_stage
tools.description: Immediately stop XY and Z stage motion and abort any z-stack or time-lapse in progress.

servers.name: New Era Syringe Pump
servers.summary: Set the syringe (presets or diameter), infuse or withdraw an exact volume at a set rate, track dispensed volume, stop.
servers.description: MCP server for New Era Pump Systems syringe pumps (NE-1000 family, RS-232): set syringe, infuse/withdraw volumes, monitor, stop.

tools.name: clear_dispensed_volume
tools.description: Reset the infused and withdrawn volume accumulators to zero. Only possible while stopped.

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: get_dispensed_volume
tools.description: Return the accumulated infused and withdrawn volumes (pump command DIS).

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Report what the pump is doing (infusing/withdrawing/stopped/paused, alarms), the syringe diameter, rate, target volume, direction and the accumulated dispensed volumes.

tools.name: infuse
tools.description: Push `volume_ml` out of the syringe at `rate_ml_min`, then stop. Returns as soon as pumping has started, with the estimated duration. Requires the correct syringe diameter (`set_syringe`) and a stopped pump. Overwrites phases 1-2 of the pump's stored Pumping Program.

tools.name: list_syringe_presets
tools.description: List the syringe inside diameters from the New Era manual's reference table (BD, Monoject, Terumo, HSW Norm-Ject, Poulten & Graf glass, stainless steel, SGE, Hamilton), with the NE-1000 rate range each allows. Use a name with `set_syringe`.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: set_syringe
tools.description: Set the syringe inside diameter, either from a preset or a measured value. The pump must be stopped. Changing the diameter also resets the dispensed-volume accumulators and may switch the pump's volume units (µL below 14.0 mm, mL above).

tools.name: stop_pump
tools.description: Stop the pump immediately (STP). A paused program is also cancelled so it cannot resume.

tools.name: withdraw
tools.description: Pull `volume_ml` into the syringe at `rate_ml_min`, then stop. Returns as soon as pumping has started. Make sure the syringe has room for the volume. Overwrites phases 1-2 of the pump's stored Pumping Program.

servers.name: Opentrons OT-2 / Flex
servers.summary: Upload and analyze protocols, review deck layout, start/pause/stop/resume runs, track progress, home, lights, read pipettes and modules, switch modules off.
servers.description: MCP server for Opentrons OT-2 and Flex liquid-handling robots (HTTP API): upload and analyze protocols, start, pause and stop runs, monitor progress, modules and pipettes.

tools.name: deactivate_modules
tools.description: Switch attached modules off: stop heating/cooling (Temperature Module, Thermocycler block and lid, Heater-Shaker heater), stop shaking, and lower Magnetic Module magnets. Only possible when no run is in progress: stop the run first.

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: get_protocol
tools.description: Show a stored protocol's analysis: whether it is ready to run, analysis errors, the deck layout it expects (labware and modules per slot, pipettes per mount, liquids), the number of steps and the highest module temperature / shake speed it requests. Review this with the user before start_run.

tools.name: get_robot_status
tools.description: Report the robot's name, model (Flex/OT-2), software and firmware versions, lights, door and E-stop state, and the current run. Call this first to check the robot is ready.

tools.name: get_run_status
tools.description: Report a run's status, the step it is on, progress, recent steps and any errors, plus advice on what to do next (e.g. when the run is waiting for error recovery).

tools.name: home_robot
tools.description: Home all axes of the robot (the gantry and pipettes move to their home positions). Refused while a run is active. Make sure nothing is in the robot's path and the door is closed.

tools.name: list_instruments
tools.description: List attached pipettes (and the Flex gripper): mount, name, channels, volume range, and whether a tip is detected and calibration data exists.

tools.name: list_modules
tools.description: List attached modules (Temperature Module, Heater-Shaker, Thermocycler, Magnetic Module, Absorbance Plate Reader, ...) with live temperatures, targets, shake speed and status.

tools.name: list_protocols
tools.description: List protocols stored on the robot (newest last) with their analysis status and result.

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description: List recent protocol runs, newest first, with their status.

tools.name: pause_run
tools.description: Pause a running protocol. The robot finishes its current step and then holds; resume_run continues it.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: resume_run
tools.description: Resume a paused run (the robot starts moving again), or leave error recovery. Refused while the door is open. For a run awaiting recovery, `error_recovery` must be given.

tools.name: set_lights
tools.description: Turn the robot's deck (rail) lights on or off.

tools.name: start_run
tools.description: Create a run of an analyzed protocol and start it: the robot begins moving and pipetting. Refused unless the protocol's analysis completed without errors, its module setpoints are within the safety limits, no other run is active, the door is closed and the E-stop is released.

tools.name: stop_run
tools.description: Stop (cancel) a run immediately. A stopped run cannot be resumed; the robot homes and drops any attached tips into the trash. Use this whenever something looks wrong.

tools.name: upload_protocol
tools.description: Upload a protocol file (plus optional custom labware) to the robot. The robot analyzes it (simulates it) and this tool returns the analysis: errors, deck layout and whether it is ready to run. Uploading does not move the robot. Uploading identical files returns the existing protocol.

servers.name: Tecan Cavro Syringe Pump
servers.summary: Initialize, aspirate and dispense microlitre volumes at set flow rates, switch valve ports, read plunger/valve status, terminate moves.
servers.description: MCP server for Tecan Cavro syringe pumps (XLP 6000, XMP 6000, XCalibur) over the DT protocol: initialize, aspirate/dispense µL, switch valve ports, terminate.

tools.name: aspirate_ul
tools.description: Draw `volume_ul` into the syringe at `flow_ul_s` through the current (or given) valve port, and wait until the move has finished. The pump must be initialized and have room for the volume.

tools.name: dispense_ul
tools.description: Push `volume_ul` out of the syringe at `flow_ul_s` through the current (or given) valve port, and wait until the move has finished. The syringe must contain at least that volume.

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Report whether the pump is ready or busy, any error (decoded), the plunger position as the volume in the syringe, the valve position, resolution mode and current top speed.

tools.name: initialize
tools.description: Initialize the pump: drive the plunger to the top of the syringe (expelling its contents through the valve), set that as position 0 and home the valve. Needed after power-up, a plunger overload or `terminate`. Route the valve output to waste first. Takes a few seconds.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: set_valve
tools.description: Turn the valve to a named position (3/4-port valves) or to a numbered port (distribution valves). In bypass the plunger cannot move. Returns the new status.

tools.name: terminate
tools.description: Stop any plunger move, loop or delay immediately (DT command T). A valve move in progress still completes. Re-initialize afterwards: the plunger may have lost steps.

servers.name: IKA Hotplate & Overhead Stirrer
servers.summary: Read plate/probe temperature and speed, set and start heating and stirring, hardware watchdog, wait for temperature, stop all.
servers.description: MCP server for IKA hotplate stirrers and overhead stirrers (NAMUR commands): heat, stir, watchdog, wait for temperature.

tools.name: disable_watchdog
tools.description: Cancel watchdog mode 2 (OUT_WD2@0) and stop the background refresh. Watchdog mode 1 has no cancel command; this tool reports an error for it.

tools.name: enable_watchdog
tools.description: Arm the hotplate's communication watchdog (OUT_WD1@m / OUT_WD2@m). The server then re-sends the watchdog command in the background; if the computer, this server or the cable fails, the hotplate switches heating and stirring off (mode 1) or falls back to the given safety values (mode 2) after `timeout_s`. Note: stopping or reconnecting the server also stops the refresh, so the watchdog trips unless you enable it again. Mode 1 cannot be cancelled over the interface.

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Read temperatures, stirring speed and setpoints. On hotplates: plate and external-probe temperature, temperature setpoint and the device's safety-circuit temperature. On overhead stirrers: PT1000 probe temperature, torque and the speed/torque limits set on the device.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: set_speed
tools.description: Set the stirring speed setpoint (OUT_SP_4). Does not start the motor; if it is already running, the speed changes immediately. Refused above `max_speed_rpm` (and, on overhead stirrers, above the speed limit set on the device).

tools.name: set_temperature
tools.description: Set the hotplate temperature setpoint (OUT_SP_1). With an external probe connected this is the target temperature of the medium. Does not start heating; if heating is already on, the plate starts moving to the new setpoint immediately. Refused above `max_temperature_c` or above the device's own safety-circuit temperature.

tools.name: start_heating
tools.description: Switch the hotplate heater on (START_1). It heats towards the current setpoint, which is checked against `max_temperature_c` first. Make sure the vessel and its contents can take the setpoint temperature and that nothing flammable is near the plate.

tools.name: start_stirring
tools.description: Start the stirring motor (START_4) at the current speed setpoint, which is checked against `max_speed_rpm` first. Make sure the stir bar or impeller is in place and the vessel is secured (a decoupled stir bar or an unclamped vessel can splash).

tools.name: stop_all
tools.description: Emergency stop: switch the heater off (hotplates) and stop the motor. Every stop command is sent even if one of them fails. Also ends a running `wait_for_temperature`.

tools.name: stop_heating
tools.description: Switch the hotplate heater off (STOP_1). Stirring continues. The plate stays hot for a long time after switching off.

tools.name: stop_stirring
tools.description: Stop the stirring motor (STOP_4). Heating (if on) continues.

tools.name: wait_for_temperature
tools.description: Poll a temperature until it is within `tolerance_c` of the target for `stable_for_s` seconds, or until `timeout_s` passes. Does not change anything on the device (start heating first). Returns whether the target was reached plus a short temperature trace. A stop command ends the wait early.

servers.name: JULABO Circulator
servers.summary: Read bath/external temperature and heating power, set setpoint, start/stop tempering, decode status and alarms, wait for temperature.
servers.description: MCP server for JULABO heating and refrigerated circulators (CORIO, MAGIO, DYNEO): read temperatures, set setpoint, start/stop, alarms.

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: get_setpoint
tools.description: Read the current temperature setpoint and whether temperature control is running.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Report the circulator's status message (decoded: operating state, rejected command or alarm), whether temperature control is running, the setpoint, the device's own excess-temperature protection setting and warning limits, and the firmware version.

tools.name: read_temperatures
tools.description: Read the bath temperature, the heating/cooling power in % and the safety-sensor temperature, and optionally the external Pt100 sensor.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: set_setpoint
tools.description: Set the circulator's temperature setpoint (out_sp_00). If temperature control is running, the circulator starts heating or cooling to it immediately. Refused outside `min_temperature_c`..`max_temperature_c`; the circulator itself also rejects values outside its range or warning limits (reported as an error). Needs remote control enabled.

tools.name: start_circulation
tools.description: Start temperature control (out_mode_05 1): the pump runs and the bath heats or cools to the setpoint, which is checked against the safety limits first (it may have been changed on the front panel). Make sure the bath is filled and any external hoses are connected and secured. Needs remote control enabled.

tools.name: stop_circulation
tools.description: Stop temperature control and the pump (out_mode_05 0), then confirm with in_mode_05. Also ends a running `wait_for_temperature`. The bath stays hot/cold after stopping.

tools.name: wait_for_temperature
tools.description: Poll the bath (or external) temperature until it has been within `tolerance_c` of the target for `stable_for_s` seconds, or `timeout_s` passes. Does not change anything; start circulation first. Stops early (reached = false) if the circulator raises an alarm or a stop command is sent. Returns a short temperature trace.

servers.name: Mettler Toledo Balance
servers.summary: Weigh (stable/immediate), tare, zero, log drift series, internal adjustment, draft shield, display messages.
servers.description: MCP server for Mettler Toledo laboratory balances (MT-SICS): weigh, tare, zero, log drift, adjust.

tools.name: clear_tare
tools.description: Clear the tare memory (tare = 0).

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: get_draft_shield
tools.description: Report the position of the motorised draft-shield doors (Excellence/XPR balances only).

tools.name: get_tare
tools.description: Return the weight currently stored in the tare memory.

tools.name: log_weight_series
tools.description: Record a series of immediate (unfiltered) readings to monitor drift, evaporation, moisture uptake or stabilisation. Returns every reading plus summary statistics.

tools.name: read_temperature
tools.description: Read the balance's internal temperature probe(s) in °C (MT-SICS M28, if supported).

tools.name: read_weight
tools.description: Read the current net weight from the balance.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: reset_balance
tools.description: Abort whatever the balance is doing (an adjustment, a repeating weight stream, a pending command) and reset it to its power-on state without zeroing (MT-SICS @). Clears the tare. Motorised draft-shield doors have their own obstruction detection and reverse if blocked.

tools.name: run_internal_adjustment
tools.description: Adjust (calibrate) the balance with its built-in reference weight (MT-SICS C3). The pan must be empty and the balance undisturbed. Takes roughly 1-3 minutes.

tools.name: set_draft_shield
tools.description: Open or close the motorised draft-shield doors. Make sure nothing (and no one's fingers) is in the way of the doors.

tools.name: set_tare_preset
tools.description: Preset a known tare weight (e.g. a container weighed earlier).

tools.name: show_message
tools.description: Show a short message on the balance display (e.g. 'Add sample 3'). Use `show_weight_display` to return to the normal weight display.

tools.name: show_weight_display
tools.description: Switch the balance display back to showing the weight.

tools.name: tare
tools.description: Tare the balance: store the current load (e.g. an empty container) as the tare weight. Returns the stored tare weight.

tools.name: zero
tools.description: Zero the balance with the current load. Also clears the tare memory.

servers.name: Mass Spectrometry Data (mzML, Bruker TDF, vendor conversion)
models: Thermo .raw, Waters .raw, Agilent .d, SCIEX .wiff/.wiff2, Shimadzu .lcd, Bruker BAF (via conversion)
servers.protocol: mzML / mzMLb (pyteomics) / Bruker TDF (SQLite + timsrust) / msconvert & ThermoRawFileParser
servers.summary: Read and analyse LC-MS data from any vendor via open formats: find runs, run metadata, TIC/BPC, XICs with apex and area, spectra, MS2 search by precursor, quick QC, and conversion of vendor files with the user's own msconvert or ThermoRawFileParser.
servers.description: MCP server for mass-spectrometry data files (mzML, mzMLb, Bruker timsTOF TDF; vendor files via msconvert/ThermoRawFileParser): run info, TIC/BPC, XICs, spectra, MS2 search, QC.

tools.name: convert_to_mzml
tools.description: Convert a vendor file (Thermo .raw, Waters .raw, Agilent .d, SCIEX .wiff, Shimadzu .lcd, Bruker .d) to mzML with the converter the user installed (ThermoRawFileParser, ProteoWizard msconvert, or msconvert in Docker; chosen with --option converter=...). Writes a new file in the data folder. Can take minutes; fails with install instructions if no converter is set up.

tools.name: extract_ion_chromatogram
tools.description: Extracted ion chromatogram (XIC/EIC) for one or more m/z values: the summed intensity within ± tolerance (ppm or Da) in every MS1 spectrum (or another `ms_level`). For each target returns the apex RT and intensity, the apex peak's boundaries, area (intensity x min, no baseline subtraction) and FWHM, plus a downsampled trace. Reads every spectrum in the RT window, so restrict `rt_start_min`/`rt_end_min` on long runs.

tools.name: find_ms2_scans
tools.description: Find the MS2 (MSn) spectra whose precursor m/z is within ± tolerance of `precursor_mz`, optionally within an RT window and for one charge state. Returns index, scan number, RT, precursor m/z, error in ppm, charge and intensity; open any hit with get_spectrum.

tools.name: get_bpc
tools.description: Base peak chromatogram (intensity of the most intense peak per spectrum, with its m/z) vs retention time, downsampled to `max_points`. Cleaner than the TIC for spotting eluting compounds; the base-peak m/z tells you which ion dominates each part of the run.

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: get_run_info
tools.description: Describe one run: instrument vendor/model/serial (when the file records them), acquisition date, software, number of spectra per MS level, retention-time and m/z ranges, polarity, centroid/profile, and whether ion-mobility data is present. The first call on a large file indexes it (can take a while); later calls are instant.

tools.name: get_spectrum
tools.description: Read one spectrum, chosen by `index`, `scan_number`, `native_id` or nearest `rt_min` (give exactly one). Returns MS level, RT, polarity, centroid/profile, precursor m/z and charge for MS2, a summary (peak count, TIC, base peak, m/z range) and the `top_n` most intense peaks; `save_path` writes the full peak list to CSV. For profile spectra the top peaks are local maxima of the profile.

tools.name: get_tic
tools.description: Total ion chromatogram (sum of all intensities per spectrum vs retention time) for one MS level, downsampled to `max_points` (keeping the maximum in each bin so peaks survive). Returns the apex, median and area; `save_path` writes every point to CSV.

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description: Find mass-spectrometry runs in the data folder and detect each one's vendor and format (mzML/mzML.gz/mzMLb, Bruker .d TDF or BAF, Agilent .d, Thermo .raw, Waters .raw folder, SCIEX .wiff/.wiff2, Shimadzu .lcd, mzXML). `readable_directly=false` means the run must be converted with convert_to_mzml before it can be analysed.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: summarise_run
tools.description: Quick QC of a run: MS1/MS2 counts, TIC stability (CV, spray dropouts), where the signal elutes, cycle time, MS2 scans per cycle, median injection times and how often MS2 hit the maximum injection time, and precursor charge states. Returns plain-language warnings.

servers.name: LC-MS Worklist Builder

servers.summary: Build, randomise, validate, convert and export LC-MS sample queues as vendor import files (never starts a run).
servers.description: MCP server that builds, validates and exports LC-MS worklist import files for MassLynx, SCIEX OS, MassHunter and Xcalibur.

tools.name: add_samples
tools.description: Append samples to a draft worklist (the worklist's defaults and automatic positions apply; any blank/QC/randomisation plan is re-applied to the longer list with the same seed).

tools.name: create_worklist
tools.description: Create an in-memory draft worklist from a sample list plus defaults (methods, injection volume, tray positions, data-file naming pattern). Nothing is written to disk until export_worklist. Injection volumes above the max_injection_volume_ul limit are refused.

tools.name: export_worklist
tools.description: Validate the draft and write the vendor import file into the output folder. Returns the path, a preview of the first lines, warnings and import instructions. Refuses if validation finds errors or the file exists (unless overwrite=true). This does not start an acquisition: a person imports the file into the acquisition software.

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: get_worklist
tools.description: Show a draft worklist in run order, with its defaults, blank/QC plan, randomisation seed and the history of operations applied to it.

tools.name: import_worklist
tools.description: Parse an existing MassLynx, SCIEX OS, MassHunter or Xcalibur import file from the output folder into a draft, so it can be validated, edited or exported in another vendor's format. Columns without a neutral equivalent are kept verbatim. Only reads; nothing is written.

tools.name: insert_qc_blanks
tools.description: Insert blanks and QC injections and optionally randomise the run order (with a recorded seed). Replaces any previous plan, so calling it again does not duplicate blanks. The plan is re-applied whenever samples are added; data-file names follow the new run order.

tools.name: list_formats
tools.description: List the supported import formats (Waters MassLynx, SCIEX OS, Agilent MassHunter, Thermo Xcalibur): columns, required fields, sample-type names, file extensions, how to import, what is verified against vendor documents and what is assumed, and the source URLs. Also lists the position patterns and the formats that were researched but not implemented.

tools.name: list_worklists
tools.description: List the draft worklists in memory and the files in the output folder.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: validate_worklist
tools.description: Check a draft against the target format: required fields, duplicate data-file names, characters Windows does not allow in file names, tray/vial position format and plate bounds, injection volume (> 0 and <= the max_injection_volume_ul limit), and method file extensions. Errors block export; warnings don't.

servers.name: Ocean Insight Spectrometer
servers.summary: Acquire averaged/smoothed spectra with saturation checks, auto integration time, dark and reference storage, absorbance and transmittance spectra, peak positions with FWHM, detector TEC (QE Pro).
servers.description: MCP server for Ocean Insight / Ocean Optics spectrometers (python-seabreeze): acquire spectra, auto integration time, dark/reference, absorbance and transmittance, peak finding.

tools.name: acquire_spectrum
tools.description: Acquire an intensity spectrum (raw counts) with optional averaging, boxcar smoothing and corrections. Returns downsampled (wavelength, counts), summary statistics, the most prominent peaks with FWHM, and a saturation check; `save_path` writes the full spectrum to a new .csv file (an existing file is never overwritten).

tools.name: auto_integration_time
tools.description: Adjust the integration time until the brightest raw pixel (optionally within a wavelength window) is within the target band of saturation (default 70-85 %). Stays within the device limits and the `max_integration_time_ms` safety limit. Re-take dark/reference afterwards.

tools.name: detector_cooling_off
tools.description: Switch the detector thermo-electric cooler off (the detector warms to ambient). Does nothing on spectrometers without a TEC.

tools.name: find_peaks
tools.description: Find peaks (or dips) with position, height, prominence and FWHM in the most recent spectrum (intensity, absorbance or transmittance). Acquires a fresh intensity spectrum if none has been taken yet.

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: get_device_info
tools.description: Model, serial, pixel count, wavelength range, integration-time limits, saturation level, supported corrections, TEC presence, and which dark/reference spectra are stored.

tools.name: list_spectrometers
tools.description: List the Ocean spectrometers seabreeze can see (model, serial number, whether open) and which one this server is connected to. Use a serial number as `--address` to pick one.

tools.name: measure_absorbance
tools.description: Measure the absorbance spectrum A = -log10((S - D) / (R - D)) of the sample now in the beam, using the stored dark D and reference R (same settings). Ask the user to insert the sample first. Also returns values at `wavelengths_nm` and the absorbance maxima.

tools.name: measure_transmittance
tools.description: Measure the transmittance spectrum %T = 100 (S - D) / (R - D) of the sample now in the beam, using the stored dark and reference. Ask the user to insert the sample first. Also returns values at `wavelengths_nm` and the deepest transmission dips.

tools.name: read_detector_temperature
tools.description: Read the detector temperature from the thermo-electric cooler (TE-cooled models such as the QE Pro, when seabreeze exposes the thermo_electric feature for them).

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: set_detector_cooling
tools.description: Enable the detector thermo-electric cooler at `setpoint_c` (TE-cooled models only). The detector takes minutes to settle; dark current (and noise) drops as it cools. The TEC can only cool to roughly 15-40 °C below ambient (QE Pro manual). Checked against `min_tec_setpoint_c`.

tools.name: set_integration_time
tools.description: Set the detector integration time (ms), within the device limits from `get_device_info`. Stored dark/reference spectra become unusable until re-taken at the new time.

tools.name: store_dark_reference
tools.description: Record and store a DARK spectrum (kept in memory) for absorbance/transmittance. BEFORE calling, ask the user to BLOCK THE LIGHT PATH (close the shutter, switch the lamp off or cap the fiber) and wait for confirmation. Uses the present integration time.

tools.name: store_reference
tools.description: Record and store the REFERENCE (100 % transmission) spectrum in memory. BEFORE calling, ask the user to put the BLANK (solvent-filled or empty cuvette) in the beam with the light on, and wait for confirmation. Use the same settings as the dark.

servers.name: PalmSens Potentiostat
servers.protocol: MethodSCRIPT v1.x + PalmSens online communication protocol
servers.summary: Cyclic, linear-sweep and differential-pulse voltammetry, chronoamperometry and raw MethodSCRIPT, with peak summaries and CSV export.
servers.description: MCP server for PalmSens potentiostats running MethodSCRIPT (EmStat Pico, EmStat4, Sensit, Nexus): CV, LSV, DPV, chronoamperometry, raw scripts.

tools.name: abort_measurement
tools.description: Abort the running measurement or script immediately (communication command Z) and make sure the cell is switched off. Safe to call when nothing is running.

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: get_device_info
tools.description: Identify the potentiostat (model, firmware, serial number) and list its potential window, PGStat modes and current ranges, so measurement parameters can be chosen within them.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: run_chronoamperometry
tools.description: Hold the cell at `potential_v` for `run_time_s` and record the current every `interval_s`. Returns the data (time from the instrument timer) plus first/last/mean current and the charge. Applies potential to the cell.

tools.name: run_cyclic_voltammetry
tools.description: Run a cyclic voltammogram: begin -> vertex 1 -> vertex 2 -> begin, `n_scans` times, and return potential/current/time data with the anodic and cathodic peaks of every scan. Applies potential to the cell for the whole scan; the cell is switched off at the end.

tools.name: run_differential_pulse_voltammetry
tools.description: Run differential pulse voltammetry (current = forward - reverse, per step) from begin to end potential and return the data with the peak current and peak potential. The scan rate must be below step / pulse_time / 2. Applies potential to the cell.

tools.name: run_linear_sweep_voltammetry
tools.description: Run a linear sweep voltammogram from `begin_potential_v` to `end_potential_v` and return the data with the largest/smallest current and where they occur. Applies potential to the cell.

tools.name: run_methodscript
tools.description: Advanced: run a raw MethodSCRIPT and return its raw output and decoded data packages. Literal potentials of set_e / set_range_minmax da and the CV, LSV, DPV, SWV, NPV, ACV, CA, PAD, EIS and fast CV/CA techniques are checked against `max_potential_v`, and literal `set_range ba` / `set_autoranging ba` currents against `max_current_range_a`; values computed at run time are not. Aborted after `timeout_s`; add `on_finished:` + `cell_off` to your script so the cell is switched off after an abort. After a runtime error, a timeout or `abort_measurement` the server switches the cell off itself.

servers.name: Sartorius Balance
servers.summary: Weigh (stable/immediate), tare, zero, log drift series, internal adjustment, ambient filter, keypad lock.
servers.description: MCP server for Sartorius laboratory balances (SBI protocol): weigh, tare, zero, log drift, internal adjustment.

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: lock_keypad
tools.description: Block or unblock the balance keys, e.g. so nobody tares by accident during a long logging run.

tools.name: log_weight_series
tools.description: Record a series of immediate (unfiltered) readings to monitor drift, evaporation, moisture uptake or stabilisation. Returns every reading plus summary statistics.

tools.name: read_weight
tools.description: Read the current net weight from the balance (ESC P). With stable=True the server polls until the balance reports a stable value; if it cannot settle (draughts, vibration, evaporation) you get an error; retry, or use stable=false for the current value.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: run_internal_adjustment
tools.description: Adjust (calibrate) the balance with its built-in weight (ESC Z; isoCAL models only). The pan must be empty and the balance undisturbed. SBI sends no completion message, so the server watches for the adjustment status and waits until the balance weighs again; check `observed_adjustment` and the balance display or GLP printout for the result.

tools.name: set_ambient_conditions
tools.description: Adapt the balance's filter to the ambient conditions (ESC K/L/M/N). Use 'unstable' or 'very_unstable' for draughty or vibrating benches (slower but steadier readings).

tools.name: tare
tools.description: Tare the balance (ESC U, or ESC T on legacy balances): the current load (e.g. an empty container) becomes the tare. Then waits for a stable reading and checks that it is ~0; returns that reading.

tools.name: zero
tools.description: Zero the balance (ESC V). Only works with the pan (nearly) empty, within the balance's zero-setting range; clears the tare. Confirms by reading ~0 afterwards.

servers.name: Thermo Orbitrap (Instrument API)
servers.summary: Adapter for the licensed Thermo IAPI (bring your own assemblies): instrument status, live scan buffer with MS-order filters, validated and rate-limited custom and repeating scans, acquisitions to raw files, stop/cancel.
servers.description: MCP server adapter for Thermo Fisher Orbitrap mass spectrometers via the licensed Instrument API (IAPI): status, live scans, custom and repeating scans, acquisitions.

tools.name: cancel_custom_scans
tools.description: Cancel any pending custom scan and its processing delay (IAPI CancelCustomScan).

tools.name: cancel_repeating_scan
tools.description: Cancel the repeating scan set with set_repeating_scan (IAPI CancelRepetition).

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: get_instrument_status
tools.description: Report the instrument model, IAPI service/instrument connection, system mode and state (On/Standby/Off; Running/ReadyToDownload/...), whether an acquisition can be paused or resumed, the IAPI licence where the API exposes it, requested readbacks, the latest scan status log (vacuum, source) and how many scans have arrived.

tools.name: get_possible_scan_parameters
tools.description: List the scan parameters this instrument accepts for custom and repeating scans (IScans.PossibleParameters): name, allowed range or choices, default and help. The set depends on the model, licence and Tune version.

tools.name: get_recent_scans
tools.description: Return the most recent scans received from the instrument (oldest first), optionally only one MS order or one custom scan's access id: scan number, MS order, precursor m/z, AGC target, injection time and the most intense centroids. Scans only arrive in On mode.

tools.name: pause_acquisition
tools.description: Pause the running acquisition (IAPI Pause). Fails if the instrument reports it cannot pause.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: resume_acquisition
tools.description: Resume a paused acquisition (IAPI Resume). Sample consumption continues.

tools.name: set_repeating_scan
tools.description: Define or replace the scan the instrument repeats when no method or custom scan is running (IAPI CreateRepeatingScan/SetRepetitionScan). Values are validated like submit_custom_scan. Cancel with cancel_repeating_scan.

tools.name: start_acquisition
tools.description: Start an acquisition with the instrument's current settings (IAPI StartAcquisition), recording to a raw file. This consumes sample. The instrument must be On; an acquisition must not already be running. Stop it with stop_acquisition. scan_count and until_stopped acquisitions are cancelled automatically after max_acquisition_duration_s.

tools.name: stop_acquisition
tools.description: Stop the running acquisition (IAPI CancelAcquisition), by default also cancelling custom and repeating scans, and optionally switch the instrument to Standby (switch back to On in Tune). Every step is attempted even if an earlier one fails; failures are reported.

tools.name: submit_custom_scan
tools.description: Place one custom scan to run next (IAPI CreateCustomScan/SetCustomScan); unset values fall back to the instrument's defaults. Every value is checked against PossibleParameters and the safety limits, and calls are rate-limited, before anything is sent. Fetch the result with wait_for_scan(access_id=running_number).

tools.name: wait_for_scan
tools.description: Wait for the next scan that arrives after this call (optionally of one MS order, or the result of a custom scan by its access id) and return it. For a custom scan placed with submit_custom_scan, a result that arrived since it was placed is returned at once. Returns found=false after timeout_s if nothing matching arrived (e.g. the instrument is in Standby).

servers.name: Alicat Mass Flow & Pressure Controller
servers.summary: Read mass/volumetric flow, pressure and temperature, set setpoints, select gases, tare, hold or close valves, log flow series.
servers.description: MCP server for Alicat mass flow and pressure meters/controllers: read flow, set setpoints, select gas, tare, hold/close valves.

tools.name: close_valve
tools.description: Stop the flow: set the flow setpoint to 0 and hold all valves closed (Alicat HC). Safe to call at any time. On pressure controllers the pressure setpoint is left unchanged and the valves are held closed, trapping the current pressure.

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: get_device_info
tools.description: Report model, serial number, firmware, calibration date, whether the device is a controller, the units of every data-frame field, the setpoint full scale and setpoint source.

tools.name: hold_valve
tools.description: Freeze the controller's valve(s) at their current position (HLD): closed-loop control stops, so flow will drift if upstream pressure changes. Use `resume_control` to release, or `close_valve` to shut off completely.

tools.name: list_gases
tools.description: List the gases installed on this mass flow device (number and short name), as used by `set_gas`. Liquid and pressure-only devices have no gas list.

tools.name: log_flow_series
tools.description: Record a time series of data frames (e.g. to check flow stability, settling after a setpoint change, or pressure drift). Returns every point plus mean/stdev/min/max of the mass flow (or the main measured quantity for non-flow devices).

tools.name: read_flow
tools.description: Read the live data frame: mass flow, volumetric flow, pressure, temperature, setpoint (controllers), active gas and any status codes, each with the device's engineering units.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: resume_control
tools.description: Cancel any valve hold and resume closed-loop control to the current setpoint. Flow restarts immediately if the setpoint is not 0 (check it with `read_flow` first).

tools.name: set_flow_setpoint
tools.description: Change the controller setpoint: starts, changes or stops gas flow (or sets the target pressure on a pressure controller). 0 stops flow and closes the valve on a flow controller. Negative values only work on bidirectional controllers. Refused on meters, above the `max_setpoint` limit, and above the device's full scale.

tools.name: set_gas
tools.description: Select the gas calibration the mass flow device uses (Gas Select). This changes how flow is computed, so do it with the setpoint at 0. Only gases installed on the device work (see `list_gases`); corrosive gases need anti-corrosive (S-series) hardware.

tools.name: tare_flow
tools.description: Tare (zero) the flow reading. ONLY run with no flow through the device: upstream shut off or controller setpoint 0, with the line at its normal operating pressure. Refused if the setpoint is not 0 or a significant flow is still being measured.

tools.name: tare_pressure
tools.description: Tare a pressure reading. Requires no flow and the device OPEN TO ATMOSPHERE (gauge), or no flow and an unpressurised process line (absolute, barometer-equipped devices only).

servers.name: Bench DC Power Supply
servers.protocol: SCPI (Rigol, Siglent) and Aim-TTi remote commands
servers.summary: Read setpoints and measured V/I/CV-CC per channel, set voltage and current limits, switch outputs on/off, set OVP/OCP, read errors.
servers.description: MCP server for programmable DC bench power supplies (Rigol DP700/DP800/DP900, Siglent SPD3303X/SPD1000X, Aim-TTi CPX/MX/QL/PL-P): set, measure, switch outputs, OVP/OCP.

tools.name: all_outputs_off
tools.description: Switch every output OFF (emergency stop for the whole supply). Each channel is switched individually and read back where the instrument supports it.

tools.name: clear_protection_trip
tools.description: Clear an OVP/OCP trip after fixing its cause. The output stays OFF; use `output_on` to re-energise. On Aim-TTi supplies this clears trips on all outputs.

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: get_errors
tools.description: Read (and clear) the instrument's error queue / error registers. Empty list = no errors.

tools.name: get_outputs
tools.description: Report each channel: voltage and current-limit setpoints, measured voltage/current/power, output on/off, CV/CC mode, and OVP/OCP levels and trip state where the model supports them.

tools.name: output_off
tools.description: Switch a channel's output OFF. Safe to call at any time.

tools.name: output_on
tools.description: Switch a channel's output ON, energising the connected load at the present setpoints. The setpoints are read back first and the output is refused if they exceed the safety limits (e.g. after someone changed them on the front panel).

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: set_current_limit
tools.description: Set a channel's current limit (the constant-current setpoint). Refused above `max_current_a` (checked even with the output off) or above the channel's range.

tools.name: set_protection
tools.description: Set over-voltage (OVP) and/or over-current (OCP) protection for a channel. When exceeded, the supply switches the output off. Rigol: levels + on/off; Aim-TTi CPX/QL/PL-P: levels (always armed), MX: levels + on/off; Siglent SPD1000X: levels only; SPD3303X: not available.

tools.name: set_voltage
tools.description: Set a channel's voltage setpoint. Refused above `max_voltage_v` (checked even with the output off) or above the channel's range. If the output is on, the load sees the new voltage at once.

tools.name: read_digital_inputs

tools.name: read_thermocouple
tools.description: Read a thermocouple with the T7/T8 AIN thermocouple extended feature (types B, C, E, J, K, N, R, S, T) and return °C with the measured voltage and cold-junction temperature.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: set_digital_output
tools.description: Make a digital line an output and drive it high (3.3 V) or low (0 V).

tools.name: set_outputs_safe
tools.description: Put the outputs in a safe state: stop any stream, set DAC0 and DAC1 to 0 V, and release every digital line this server drove (plus the `safe_dio` option lines) to input - or drive them low with dio_mode='low'. Use when finished or if anything looks wrong.

tools.name: stream_analog
tools.description: Acquire a hardware-timed waveform on one or more analog inputs (LJM stream mode) and return per-channel statistics plus a downsampled waveform; optionally save everything to CSV.

tools.name: write_dac
tools.description: Set an analog output (DAC0/DAC1) to a DC voltage. The output stays at this value until changed or `set_outputs_safe` is called.

servers.name: NI-DAQmx DAQ Devices

servers.summary: List devices, acquire finite analog voltage and thermocouple data, read/write digital lines and set analog outputs, with voltage, rate and sample limits.

tools.name: list_devices

tools.name: read_analog

tools.name: read_digital_lines

tools.name: read_thermocouple

tools.name: set_outputs_safe
tools.description: Put the device's outputs in a safe state: every analog output to 0 V (or the bottom of its range if 0 V is not in it) and, by default, every digital line this server drove - plus the `safe_do_lines` option lines - driven low. Use when finished or if anything looks wrong.

tools.name: write_analog

tools.name: write_digital_lines

servers.name: Rigol Oscilloscope
servers.summary: Read settings, autoscale, run/stop/single, set channels, timebase and edge trigger, take measurements, capture scaled waveforms (screen or deep memory) and screenshots.
servers.description: MCP server for Rigol digital oscilloscopes (DS1000Z/MSO1000Z, DS1000Z-E, MSO5000, DHO800/900/1000/4000): settings, triggering, measurements, waveform capture and screenshots over SCPI.

tools.name: autoscale
tools.description: Run the scope's automatic setup (AUTO key): it picks vertical scales, timebase and trigger for the connected signals. This overwrites the user's current setup - only use it when asked. Needs signals of roughly >20 mVpp and >40 Hz.

tools.name: capture_waveform

tools.name: force_trigger

tools.name: get_settings

tools.name: measure
tools.description: Read the scope's automatic measurements for one channel: voltages (Vpp, Vmax, Vmin, Vtop, Vbase, Vamp, Vavg, Vrms, overshoot, preshoot) and timing (period, frequency, rise/fall time, +/- width, +/- duty). Values the scope cannot determine are null.

tools.name: screenshot

tools.name: set_channel

tools.name: set_timebase

tools.name: set_trigger
tools.description: Configure an edge trigger (source, level, slope) and the sweep mode. Sets the trigger type to EDGE. The level must lie within the source channel's screen range.

tools.name: single
tools.description: Arm a single acquisition (SINGLE key): the scope triggers once, then stops. With wait_s > 0 it waits until the acquisition is complete (status STOP). If the trigger condition is never met the status stays WAIT - check the trigger level/source or use `force_trigger`.

tools.name: stop
tools.description: Stop acquisition (STOP) and freeze the current waveforms, e.g. before reading deep memory.

tools.name: get_board_info

tools.description: Check every EXG channel for common electrode problems: flat line (disconnected), railed (amplifier saturated, OpenBCI Cyton boards), strong 50/60 Hz mains noise (poor contact or missing reference), and implausibly high amplitude (movement, muscle, loose electrode).

tools.name: insert_marker

tools.name: list_supported_boards

tools.name: start_streaming

servers.name: Keithley SourceMeter SMU
servers.summary: Configure a voltage or current source with compliance, switch the output on/off, measure V and I, run bounded linear/log/dual IV sweeps with resistance fit and CSV export, 2/4-wire sense.
servers.description: MCP server for Keithley SourceMeter SMUs (2400 series SCPI, 2450 family SCPI, 2600B TSP): source V or I with compliance, measure, bounded IV sweeps that always end with the output off.

tools.name: configure_source
tools.description: Set up the source (function, level, compliance, range, measurement speed) while the output is OFF. Measures V and I with auto-ranging. Refused if the output is on; turn it off first or use `set_source_level`. Limits are checked before anything is sent.

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: get_device_info
tools.description: Identify the SMU: manufacturer, model, serial, firmware, command dialect (2400 / 2450 / 2600), channel (2600B) and the model's maximum source voltage and current.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Report whether the output is on, the source function (voltage/current), programmed level, compliance limit, whether the source is in compliance, terminals and 2/4-wire sense.

tools.name: measure
tools.description: Take one source-measure reading (voltage, current, V/I, power, compliance flag) of the energised DUT. Does not change any setting; refused if the output is off.

tools.name: output_off
tools.description: Switch the SMU output OFF immediately (and abort any IV sweep in progress). Always available, including in read-only mode.

tools.name: output_on
tools.description: Switch the SMU output ON: the configured voltage or current is applied to the DUT. The programmed level and compliance are read back from the instrument and checked against the safety limits first. Confirm with the user that the DUT is connected and safe to energise.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: run_iv_sweep
tools.description: Run a stepped IV sweep: configure the source, switch the output ON, step through the levels measuring V and I at each, then ALWAYS switch the output OFF (also on errors or when `output_off` is called). Returns the curve (downsampled), compliance flags, a linear fit and optional full CSV (a new file; an existing file is never overwritten). The output must be off beforehand. Limits are checked first.

tools.name: set_4wire
tools.description: Select 4-wire (remote sense, Kelvin) or 2-wire measurement. 4-wire removes lead resistance for low-resistance DUTs but needs the SENSE leads connected. Refused while the output is on.

tools.name: set_source_level
tools.description: Change the level of the configured source. If the output is ON the new voltage/current is applied to the DUT immediately. The level and the present compliance are checked against the safety limits first.

servers.description: MCP server for Lake Shore Cryotronics 335/336/350 temperature controllers: read sensors, setpoints, ramps, heater ranges, PID, wait for stability, all heaters off.

tools.name: all_heaters_off
tools.description: Turn every output off (heater range 0 on outputs 1-4), like the front-panel All Off key, and stop any running wait. Reports the read-back range of each output and `all_off`.

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: get_heater_status
tools.description: Report each output's control mode and input, heater range, output %, setpoint (and in kelvin), ramp state, PID values and heater errors (open/short). Reading a heater error clears it on the controller.

tools.name: read_temperatures
tools.description: Read every (or the selected) sensor input: kelvin, raw sensor units, sensor type, input name and decoded reading status (invalid, under/overrange). Disabled inputs are listed with null readings.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: set_heater_range
tools.description: Set an output's heater range (each step is ~10x more power). Anything above 0 lets the output heat: in closed loop as the PID demands, in open loop at the front-panel manual output. Refused above `max_heater_range`, or if the setpoint already programmed on a closed-loop, zone or warm-up output is above `max_setpoint_k`. Start with the lowest range that can reach the setpoint.

tools.name: set_pid
tools.description: Set the P, I and D values of an output's control loop (Lake Shore conventions).

tools.name: set_ramp
tools.description: Turn setpoint ramping on or off for an output's control loop and set the rate. With ramping on, the next setpoint change moves the setpoint gradually - gentler on samples and wiring.

tools.name: set_setpoint
tools.description: Set the control setpoint of an output's loop in kelvin. If setpoint ramping is on, the setpoint moves toward the new value at the ramp rate. Heating only happens if the output is in closed-loop mode and its heater range is not off. Refused above `max_setpoint_k`.

tools.name: wait_for_stable_temperature
tools.description: Wait until the control input of `output` has stayed within `tolerance_k` of the setpoint (and the setpoint is no longer ramping) for `stable_for_s`, or until `timeout_s`. Returns whether it stabilised, the final temperature and a downsampled trace. Changes nothing.

servers.name: Pfeiffer Vacuum Gauge Controller
servers.summary: Read and log pressures with status per channel, identify gauges, change units, switch ionisation gauges on/off with a pressure interlock, read errors.
servers.description: MCP server for Pfeiffer Vacuum TPG 361/362/366 and TPG 261/262 gauge controllers: read and log pressures, gauge types, units, ionisation-gauge power.

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info

tools.name: get_errors
tools.description: Read (and clear) the controller's ERROR word: controller error, no hardware, inadmissible parameter or syntax error. An empty list means no error.

tools.name: get_gauge_types
tools.description: List the gauge connected to each channel (TID), what kind it is, and whether it is an ionisation gauge that is currently switched on or off (SEN).

tools.name: log_pressure_series
tools.description: Log pressures at a fixed interval (e.g. a pump-down curve, leak-up/rate-of-rise test or bake-out). Returns per-channel statistics in log-space plus a downsampled series; the full series can be written to a new CSV file (an existing file is never overwritten). Bounded by `max_log_duration_s` and 2 h per call.

tools.name: read_all_pressures
tools.description: Read every channel of the controller at once (PRX), with status per channel.

tools.name: read_pressure
tools.description: Read one gauge channel: status, pressure in the display unit and in mbar.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: set_gauge_power
tools.description: Switch an ionisation gauge (IKR, PKR, PBR, IMR) on or off (SEN). Switching a hot or cold cathode gauge on at high pressure can burn out the filament or contaminate the gauge, so switching ON is refused unless a valid reading from this gauge or `reference_channel` is at or below `max_switch_on_pressure_mbar`. Switching off may trip setpoint relays used as interlocks.

tools.name: set_unit
tools.description: Change the pressure unit used on the display and interface (UNI). Readings in mbar are always included regardless of this setting.

tools.name: switch_gauge_off
tools.description: Switch an ionisation gauge off (e.g. before venting, or if the pressure is rising). Always allowed. Note that setpoint relays assigned to this channel may change state.

servers.name: SRS Lock-in Amplifier
servers.protocol: SRS remote command set (IEEE-488.2 style ASCII)
servers.summary: Read X/Y/R/θ snapshots, set reference frequency/harmonic/phase, sine amplitude, sensitivity, time constant, auto phase/gain/range, bounded frequency sweeps.
servers.description: MCP server for Stanford Research Systems lock-in amplifiers (SR810/SR830, SR860/SR865A): read X/Y/R/θ, set reference, sensitivity and time constant, frequency sweeps.

tools.name: auto_gain
tools.description: Pick the sensitivity automatically for the present signal (SR830 AGAN / SR86x ASCL). On the SR830 AGAN does nothing when the time constant is longer than 1 s.

tools.name: auto_phase
tools.description: Run Auto Phase (APHS): shift the reference phase so that Y ≈ 0 and X ≈ R. The outputs then need several time constants to settle. Does nothing if the phase is unstable.

tools.name: auto_range
tools.description: Optimise the input stage for the present signal: SR830 Auto Reserve (ARSV) or SR86x Auto Range of the voltage input range (ARNG).

tools.name: frequency_sweep
tools.description: Step the internal reference (and SINE OUT drive) from start_hz to stop_hz, waiting for the output filter to settle at each point, and record X/Y/R/θ vs frequency - e.g. a resonance or transfer-function measurement. The drive amplitude stays at its present value. Needs the internal reference. The estimated duration must be within `max_sweep_duration_s`; `set_amplitude_minimum` stops a running sweep. `save_path` must be a new .csv file.

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: get_settings
tools.description: Report the reference (source, frequency, harmonic, phase), sine output, sensitivity, time constant/slope (with the 99 % settling time), and input configuration.

tools.name: read_outputs
tools.description: Read X, Y, R and θ as one coherent snapshot (SNAP?), with the reference frequency, sensitivity, fraction of full scale and any overloads latched since the last reading.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: set_amplitude
tools.description: Set the SINE OUT amplitude (V rms), which drives the sample or excitation circuit. Refused above the `max_amplitude_v` safety limit. Tell the user the new drive level first.

tools.name: set_amplitude_minimum
tools.description: Turn the sine output down to the instrument minimum (the lock-in's closest thing to 'output off') and stop any running frequency sweep. SR810/SR830: 4 mV rms (it cannot go to zero - disconnect the cable if the sample must see no drive). SR86x: 1 nV rms and DC level 0 V.

tools.name: set_input
tools.description: Configure the signal input: A / A-B / current, AC or DC coupling, shield float/ground and (SR86x) the voltage input range. Use DC coupling below ~160 mHz. Omitted parameters are left unchanged.

tools.name: set_reference
tools.description: Set the reference: source (internal/external), internal frequency, detection harmonic and phase shift. Omitted parameters are left unchanged. Changing the frequency also changes the frequency of the SINE OUT drive (at the current amplitude).

tools.name: set_sensitivity
tools.description: Set the sensitivity (full-scale range). The smallest available range that is at least `full_scale` is chosen, so a signal of that size does not overload. On SR810/SR830 the dynamic reserve can be set at the same time.

tools.name: set_time_constant
tools.description: Set the output filter time constant (nearest available value), and optionally the filter slope and synchronous filter. The SR830 may raise a too-short time constant to its minimum for the current slope/reserve; the returned settings show the value actually used.

servers.name: SRS Residual Gas Analyzer
servers.protocol: SRS RGA command set (ASCII commands, binary ion currents)
servers.summary: Analog and histogram spectra, partial pressures at chosen m/z, total pressure, helium leak checks, gas identification; filament, CDEM and degas with pressure interlocks.
servers.description: MCP server for SRS RGA100/200/300 residual gas analyzers: spectra, partial pressures, leak checks, filament/CDEM with pressure interlocks.

tools.name: all_off
tools.description: Put the RGA in a safe state: abort any degas, CDEM off (HV0), filament off (FL0) and quadrupole RF/DC off (MR0). Use when finished, before venting, or if anything looks wrong. It interrupts a running scan or leak check, and every step is attempted even if an earlier one fails.

tools.name: analog_scan
tools.description: Record an analog mass spectrum (SC1): the quadrupole steps through the mass range and the full peak shapes are returned (downsampled) with a peak list, the total pressure measured at the end of the scan, and optionally the full data as CSV. Use it to check peak positions and to survey unknown gases. Duration depends on the noise floor (e.g. 126 ms/amu at NF4). An existing save_path file is never overwritten.

tools.name: calibrate
tools.description: Calibrate the detector: `zero` (CA) re-zeroes the ion detector at the present noise floor and detector and corrects the RF scan table for temperature drift (seconds); `electrometer` (CL) recalibrates the electrometer's full I-V response (longer, clears all zero offsets). The quadrupole RF is switched off at the end.

tools.name: cdem_off
tools.description: Switch the electron multiplier off (HV0) and return to Faraday-cup detection. Always allowed, and it interrupts a running scan, mass measurement or leak check.

tools.name: degas
tools.description: Start an ionizer degas (DG): 20 mA of 400 eV electrons clean the ion source by electron stimulated desorption. The CDEM is switched off and left off. Degassing shortens filament life; prefer a bakeout. Refused above `max_filament_pressure_torr` and beyond `max_degas_minutes`. Returns immediately; the RGA is busy until it finishes (any command would abort it), and `filament_off` / `all_off` stop it.

tools.name: filament_off
tools.description: Switch the filament off (FL0), stopping a degas first if one is running. Always allowed, and it interrupts a running scan, mass measurement or leak check.

tools.name: get_command_log
tools.description: Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real), whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Report the RGA state: filament emission, CDEM on/off and voltage, ionizer settings, scan settings, stored sensitivity factors, and the decoded error bytes (e.g. FL6 when the overpressure protection shut the filament down). Reading the error bytes clears the communication (EC?) and CDEM (EM?) error bytes, as on the instrument.

tools.name: histogram_scan
tools.description: Record a bar-graph spectrum (HS1): one peak-locked value per integer m/z plus the total pressure. Faster than an analog scan and the usual way to follow a residual gas composition.

tools.name: identify_residual_gases
tools.description: Run a histogram scan and assign the major peaks to likely gases with a simple lookup of standard 70 eV fragment patterns: H2 (2), He (4), CH4 (16/15), H2O (18/17), N2 or CO (28, split with 14 and 12), O2 (32), Ar (40), CO2 (44), plus diagnoses such as an air leak or hydrocarbon contamination. A screening aid, not a quantitative analysis.

tools.name: leak_check
tools.description: Helium leak check: monitor m/z 4 while someone sprays helium on suspect joints, and report the baseline, every response above `threshold_factor` x baseline (start/end time, peak) and the time series. Keep the first few seconds free of helium so the baseline is clean. The response time of a real leak is a few seconds. Bounded by `max_leak_check_duration_s`.

tools.name: measure_masses
tools.description: Measure partial pressures at a list of m/z values (peak-locked single-mass measurements, MR). Fast and precise for monitoring known gases; the precision and time per mass are set by the noise floor (`set_scan_parameters`). Pressures are N2-equivalent.

tools.name: read_total_pressure
tools.description: Measure the total pressure with the RGA acting as an ionisation gauge (TP?, Faraday cup). Needs the filament on and the CDEM off. The value is N2-equivalent and can differ from a Bayard-Alpert gauge by a factor of a few, depending on the gas composition.

tools.name: reconnect
tools.description: Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

tools.name: set_cdem
tools.description: Switch the electron multiplier (CDEM) on at a given high voltage for ~100-10000x more signal. High pressure shortens CDEM life and can destroy it, so this is refused unless the pressure is below `max_cdem_pressure_torr` (RGA total pressure measured now with the Faraday cup, a recent one, or `external_pressure_torr`), and the voltage is capped by `max_cdem_voltage_v`. Total-pressure readings are disabled while the CDEM is on.

tools.name: set_filament
tools.description: Switch the filament on (or change its emission current). The filament burns out or is damaged above 1e-4 Torr, so this is refused unless the pressure is below `max_filament_pressure_torr`: pass `external_pressure_torr` from a separate gauge, or, if the filament is already on, the RGA's own total pressure is measured. The RGA's protection will also shut the filament down on overpressure (reported as FL6).

tools.name: set_scan_parameters
tools.description: Change measurement settings: noise floor (speed vs detection limit), electron energy, ion energy, focus plate voltage and analog-scan resolution. Sensitivity factors stored in the head are only valid at the default ionizer settings (70 eV, 12 eV, 90 V). After changing the noise floor the detector zero is re-adjusted automatically at the start of the next scan.
